title: Large-Area SnS Crystals by Controlled Sn-S Chemical Vapor Deposition: Growth Optimization, Morphology, and Raman Characterization
summary: Tin monosulfide (SnS) is a layered IV-VI semiconductor with strong in-plane anisotropy and promising properties for optoelectronic and ferroic applications. However, obtaining large, continuous, and morphologically well-defined SnS crystals remains challenging. Here, we report the growth of large-area SnS crystals using chemical vapor deposition with separate elemental Sn and S precursors. By controlling the precursor temperatures, source positions, substrate temperature, carrier-gas flow, and hydrogen flow, we obtain SnS crystals with lateral dimensions approaching 350 micrometers.
